findings.issue: The doc says every merge commit is pruned as `merge-no-own-diff` and that admission does the pruning. That is wrong on both counts. The seed step tells the agent to mark only a merge commit with no diff of its own, and only on a commit-range target (deep-review.yaml:330-334). frontier-admit.cjs:560 then settles any seed candidate that carries a pruneReason. A merge commit that has its own diff is not pruned.

evidence.cmd: rg -n "merge commit with no diff of its own|pruneReason" .skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-review.yaml
evidence.out:
332:      a merge commit with no diff of its own as
333:      {"pruneReason":"merge-no-own-diff"} and a generated index rebuild as
334:      {"pruneReason":"generated-artifact"}. ...

fix.old: Merge commits are pruned as `merge-no-own-diff`, and index rebuilds are pruned as `generated-artifact`.
fix.new: On a commit-range target, the seed prunes a merge commit with no diff of its own as `merge-no-own-diff` and a generated index rebuild as `generated-artifact`.

findings.issue: The doc says the extension adds M minutes to the prior duration budget. The code does something else. The new budget is max(prior budget, minutes elapsed since createdAt) + M, so a run whose elapsed time is past its budget gets elapsed + M. A run with no duration budget keeps none unless --extend-minutes is given (deep-research.yaml:519-520).

fix.old: add the `--extend-minutes=M` minutes (default: the prior budget) to the duration budget
fix.new: set the duration budget to max(prior budget, minutes elapsed since `createdAt`) plus the `--extend-minutes=M` minutes (default: the prior budget), and keep no budget on a run that had none unless `--extend-minutes` is given

findings.issue: The doc says convergence.cjs returns CONTINUE with minIterationsNotReached "while the iteration count is below the floor". The same claim is in the doc's description (line 3) and in the root feature-catalog.md (lines 204 and 208). In the code, the floor check runs only once a stop candidate exists (convergence.cjs:1191-1196). Below the floor with no candidate, the reason is noStopCandidate. Stuck recovery, convergenceModeOff and stopPolicyMaxIterations also return before the floor is checked. The check also applies only when minIterations > 1. The stop-order paragraph at line 28 of the same doc describes this correctly.

The doc says review admission uses "the same caps as research". The caps differ in two ways. The review root-children cap is max(maxChildrenPerNode, 8), against research's 6 (ROOT_CHILDREN_FLOOR at frontier-admit.cjs:61, readCaps at line 286). Review relevance also prunes any proposal whose scope falls outside the review target (frontier-admit.cjs:422), and research has no such check.

For a single run, the doc counts D as the four canonical dimensions plus each custom name. It then says a fan-out lineage sizes its budget from its share of the seed, which reads as the same D. It is not. expansiveLineageBudgets in fanout-run.cjs:339-351 calls expansiveBudget with no dimensions or maxDepth argument, so D is fixed at 4 and maxDepth at 3. Review lineage prompts also hardcode `review_dimensions: all` (fanout-run.cjs:1793, 1892). The doc does not say that custom names are left out of both the lineage budget and the lineage's dimension set.

evidence.cmd: rg -n "review_dimensions: all|A review lineage reviews the canonical four" .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs
